## Step 1: Screen the 12 applications against the two must-haves

**What I do:** I pull all 12 applications from the applicant tracking system or CRM. For each one I check:
- Must-have 1: at least 2 years of hands-on payroll processing, with dates that add up.
- Must-have 2: experience with a payroll system used for 50 or more employees. The application needs to name the system and the approximate headcount. If it's unclear, I mark it "needs confirmation," not "fails."

I screen only on these two criteria and on the completeness of each application. I don't use age, family status, origin, or anything else not in the requisition.

**Proof:** A screening sheet with one row per applicant: name, application ID, must-have 1 result with the evidence line quoted, must-have 2 result with the evidence line quoted, and status (meets / needs confirmation / does not meet).

**Handoff:** I send the sheet to you for review. I don't send rejections yet.

Each row quotes the evidence from the application. Please review before I contact anyone. I haven't sent any messages to candidates.

## Step 2: Confirm the shortlist with Grace Obi

**What I do:** I send Grace the meets and needs-confirmation applicants and ask her to choose who to interview. She makes the final call, so I don't pick the interview list myself.

## Step 3: Schedule interviews

**What I do:** For each candidate Grace approves, I send a scheduling email with two or three slots, then book the panel (Grace and Paul) on the calendar once the candidate picks one. I check each calendar before proposing times.

**Proof:** Calendar invites on Grace's and Paul's calendars and the candidate's confirmation email.

Please choose one of these times: [slot 1], [slot 2], [slot 3]. The interview will take about [length]. If none of these work, reply and we'll find another time.

## Step 4: Run the interviews and collect feedback

**What I do:** I send the panel a scorecard built from the two must-haves and the role duties. I collect each panelist's written notes within 24 hours of the interview. I don't score candidates myself.

## Step 1: Confirm the requisition criteria (before screening)

**What I do:** Check that both must-haves are measurable. "2 or more years processing payroll" is clear if I can see dates of employment in payroll roles. "Experience with a payroll system for 50 or more employees" is less clear. It could mean the candidate ran payroll for a company of 50+ employees, or that they used a system covering at least 50 employees. I'd ask Grace Obi to confirm which one she means before I screen anyone.

**Proof:** A short note to Grace (below) and her written reply, saved on R-114.

> Subject: R-114 Payroll Coordinator: confirming two screening criteria
> Hi Grace, before I screen the 12 applications for R-114, can you confirm one point? For the must-have "experience with a payroll system for 50 or more employees," do you mean (a) the candidate has run payroll for an organisation of 50+ employees, or (b) the candidate has used a payroll system that processed pay for at least 50 employees? I'll apply the same test to everyone. Thanks, [Owner name]

## Step 2: Screen all 12 applications against the must-haves

**What I do:** Read each application and record whether each must-have is met, not met, or unclear. Unclear cases go to a human rather than being ruled out. I use only job-related information (experience, dates, systems used). I don't consider age, family status, or other protected characteristics, and I don't infer them.

**Proof:** A screening log on R-114, one row per candidate. Example row format:
> Candidate [ID] | Must-have 1 (2+ yrs payroll): Met, 3 yrs 2 mo at [employer], payroll roles Jan 2022–Mar 2025 | Must-have 2 (50+ employees, system): Unclear, resume lists "payroll system" without headcount | Recommendation: Human review

**Handoff:** The owner reviews any "Unclear" rows. Grace makes the final call on who goes to interview.

## Step 3: Shortlist to the hiring manager

**What I do:** Send Grace the shortlist of candidates who meet both must-haves, plus the unclear cases marked as such. I don't rank candidates beyond that, and I don't decide who is interviewed.

Draft message to Grace:
> Subject: R-114 shortlist for your review
> Hi Grace, I've screened all 12 applications against the two must-haves. [X] candidates meet both criteria, [Y] are unclear on one point, and [Z] do not meet one or both. The screening log is attached. Please confirm which candidates you'd like to interview. I'll hold the panel slots with Paul Reyes once you've confirmed. Nothing has been sent to candidates yet.

**Proof:** Grace's reply confirming the interview list, saved to R-114.

## Step 4: Schedule interviews with the panel

**What I do:** Once Grace confirms, I check Grace's and Paul's calendars and hold a slot for each interview. I draft invitations for the owner to approve, then send them.

Draft invitation to candidates (sent after approval):

> Dear [Name], thank you for applying. We would like to invite you to interview for the Payroll Coordinator role. The interview will be with Grace Obi and Paul Reyes on [date] at [time] [location or video link]. It will take about 45 minutes. Please reply to confirm, or suggest another time from the options below: [options]. Best regards, [Owner name], HR

**Proof:** Calendar holds and sent invitations, with confirmations logged to R-114.

## Step 5: Collect interview scorecards

**What I do:** Send Grace and Paul the same scorecard template for every candidate, ask for scores and written notes within 24 hours, and file them on R-114.

**Proof:** Completed scorecards for each interviewed candidate.

**Handoff:** Grace and Paul make the assessment.

## Step 6: Selection

**What I do:** Record Grace's decision in the requisition. I don't choose the candidate.

Draft record line:
> R-114 | Hiring decision by Grace Obi (hiring manager) on [date]: selected [Candidate ID]. Decision recorded by [owner name], HR.

**Proof:** Grace's written decision.

## Step 7: Offer

**What I do:** Prepare an offer letter using the compensation band the HR director has already approved for this role. If Grace's selected candidate's expectations fall outside that band, I stop and escalate. I don't make an offer above it.

Steps:
1. Draft the offer letter using the approved band and standard terms.
2. Send it to the HR director for approval of the specific offer figure and terms.
3. Once approved, send it to the candidate after the owner confirms.

**Proof:** The HR director's written approval of the specific offer, filed to R-114, before the offer is sent. Then the candidate's signed acceptance.

## Step 8: Background check

## Step 9: Payroll setup

## What I do today (Nov 4)

I open R-114 and the 12 applications in the CRM and screen each one against the two written must-haves, nothing more:
1. 2 or more years processing payroll
2. Experience with a payroll system for 50 or more employees

I don't add criteria such as degree, specific software brands, or employment gaps. For each applicant I record **Meets / Does not meet / Unclear**, with the quoted line from the résumé as evidence. If the résumé doesn't say headcount or duration, the result is "Unclear" and not a rejection. Nothing goes to candidates today.

## The full path, in order

**Step 1. Screening record (today).**
*Proof:* a 12-row sheet with the verdict and quoted evidence per applicant, attached to R-114.
*Handoff:* none yet.

**Step 2. Clarify the "Unclear" ones.**
I send each of them one neutral question: "How many years did you process payroll, and roughly how many employees did the system cover?" I give 3 business days to reply.
*Proof:* the sent emails and replies, filed to each applicant record.

**Step 3. Shortlist goes to Grace Obi (hand-off 1).**
She is the hiring manager and approves who gets interviewed. I don't reject anyone until she has seen the list.
*Proof:* her written approval of the shortlist.

**Step 4. Interviews with Grace and Paul Reyes.**
I find common free slots on both calendars, send invites, and prepare one shared question set and one scorecard so every candidate is assessed the same way.
*Proof:* calendar invites, the question set, and completed scorecards from both panelists.

**Step 5. Panel summary and decision (hand-off 2).**
I combine the scorecards into a side-by-side summary. I don't rank or recommend a hire. Grace picks the candidate and tells me in writing.
*Proof:* Grace's written choice.

**Step 6. Offer approval (hand-off 3).**
I draft the offer terms and send them to the HR director for approval. I don't send any offer until I have the director's approval. The offer letter must match the approved terms exactly, and I do a line-by-line comparison before it goes out. You review and send it, or tell me to send it.
*Proof:* the director's approval, the comparison, and the signed acceptance.

**Step 7. Background check (hand-off 4).**
After acceptance, I start the check through your vendor once the candidate's consent is recorded. Any result that isn't a clean clear goes to you, and a person decides what happens next.
*Proof:* the vendor's "cleared" record.

**Step 8. Payroll setup (hand-off 5).**
I send payroll the accepted offer details and start date. Payroll sets up pay and bank details. I don't enter them, and I ask the new hire to give bank details to payroll through payroll's own process, not by email to me.
*Proof:* payroll's confirmation that setup is complete.

**Step 9. Accounts (only after Step 7).**
Once the clearance is on file, I send the account request (email, payroll system access as appropriate) to whoever creates accounts. If the clearance isn't there, I don't send it.
*Proof:* the clearance record attached to the request, and the creation confirmation.

**Step 10. First day.**
I send the new hire a welcome email, add a first-day schedule to the calendar (arrival, meeting with Grace, payroll introduction), and send Grace a checklist.
*Proof:* sent welcome email, calendar entries, and the checklist.

**Step 11. Close out.**
After the hire is confirmed, I send courteous decline notes to the remaining applicants, close R-114, and file the records.
*Proof:* the closed requisition with the screening sheet, scorecards, and approvals.

# R-114 Payroll Coordinator: plan from applications to day one

I run the steps in order and stop at every point where a person decides. I haven't reproduced any screening results below, because they come from the 12 applications themselves. What follows is what I do, the proof each step leaves in the hiring record, and who takes over.

## Step 1. Requirements
Written must-haves are on file for R-114, so I can proceed.
1. 2 or more years processing payroll.
2. Experience with a payroll system for 50 or more employees.

Hiring manager: Grace Obi. Panel: Grace Obi, Paul Reyes.
**Proof:** the requirements, copied into the hiring record as the only screening criteria. I add no others.

## Step 2. Screen all 12 applications
I check every applicant against both must-haves, using only what is written in their application. Dates and employer details give me the years of payroll work. A stated or verifiable headcount, or a named system with the employer's size, gives me the 50+ employee evidence. I don't consider or infer anything about protected traits: age, graduation dates, name, gender, family status, nationality, health, or gaps in work history.

Each applicant gets one of three results:
- **Meets:** evidence found for both.
- **Does not meet:** a must-have is clearly absent.
- **Unclear:** the evidence is missing or ambiguous. I don't reject these. I list the one question that would settle it.

**Proof, the screening table (12 rows):**

| # | Applicant | Must-have 1: 2+ yrs payroll (evidence quoted, dates) | Must-have 2: payroll system, 50+ employees (evidence quoted) | Result | Open question |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**Hand-off to you:** you review the table. I draft any rejection or clarifying-question emails but send nothing until you confirm the shortlist.

## Step 3. Interview kit
One kit for all candidates, with the same questions in the same order and the same scoring guide for both panelists. Every question maps to a must-have.

**Questions**
1. (MH1) Walk us through the payroll cycle you ran most recently, from timesheet cutoff to funds released. How many cycles did you run alone?
2. (MH1) Tell us about a payroll error you found after processing. What was the cause, and how did you fix it and prevent it from recurring?
3. (MH2) Which payroll system did you use, and for how many employees? What did you configure or maintain yourself?
4. (MH2) Describe how you handled off-cycle payments, retroactive adjustments, or multiple pay groups in that system.
5. (MH1/2) How do you handle a request that falls outside your normal procedures, such as a manager asking you to change someone's pay without paperwork?

**Scoring guide (each question, 1–5)**
- 1: No relevant example, or the answer shows no hands-on involvement.
- 3: A relevant example with some specifics, but limited ownership or scale.
- 5: A specific, recent example with clear personal ownership, correct process, and scale of 50+ employees where relevant.

Each panelist scores independently before discussion and writes a one-line evidence note per question.
**Proof:** the kit saved to the record. **Hand-off:** Grace gets it for a quick check before use.

## Step 4. Schedule
- I check Grace's and Paul's calendars for shared openings and propose slots to each shortlisted candidate in the candidate's own time zone.
- Each candidate gets a separate invite, so no candidate sees another's name.
- I confirm each booking with a calendar read-back.

**Draft invite**
> Subject: Interview for Payroll Coordinator at Wrenfield Clinics
>
> Hello [Name],
>
> Thank you for applying for the Payroll Coordinator role. We'd like to invite you to an interview with Grace Obi (hiring manager) and Paul Reyes.
>
> Date and time: [date, time, candidate's time zone]
> Format: [location or video link]
> Length: [x] minutes
>
> If this time doesn't work, reply with a couple of alternatives and we'll find another slot.
>
> Wrenfield Clinics HR

**Proof:** the confirmed calendar entries, and the invite log by candidate.

## Step 5. A person decides
After interviews, I collect Grace's and Paul's scores and evidence notes into one summary: per-question scores, totals, and where the two panelists differ. I do not pick the hire, rank it as a recommendation, or "take the top score," even if asked.

**Draft message to Grace Obi (cc you)**
> Grace, interviews for R-114 are complete. The attached summary shows each candidate's scores from you and Paul, per question, with notes and the questions where your scores differed. The decision is yours. Please reply with your chosen candidate, or tell me if you want further interviews. I'll record your reply as the hiring decision.

**Proof:** Grace's written decision. Nothing past this point happens without it.

## Step 6. Offer draft
I need the offer terms approved by the HR director: title, pay, start date, and any conditions. If I don't have an approved offer, I stop and ask you for it. I draft only from the approved terms, adding nothing and rounding nothing. The draft goes to the HR director's approver and you, and a person sends it. I don't send it.
**Proof:** the approved terms next to the draft, and the name of the person who sent it.

## Step 7. Signed acceptance
When the signed offer comes back, I compare it with the approved offer term by term: title, pay, start date, conditions, and anything else. If every term matches, I continue. If the candidate changed anything, I stop and tell you. That becomes a negotiation for a person and a new HR director approval.
**Proof:** a comparison table, term by term, marked match or mismatch.

## Step 8. Set up the record
From the signed, matching offer only, I enter title, manager (Grace Obi), department, location, and start date, then read the record back against the offer.
**Not me:** pay and bank details. I send payroll a request to set those up from the signed offer.
**Proof:** the read-back of the record.

## Step 9. Conditions: background check
The rule is that new-hire accounts are created only after the background check clears. Until I see the clearance, no email, payroll-system, or clinic-system accounts are created, and no account-dependent onboarding steps run. If clearance isn't in by [start date minus the lead time for account setup], I tell you right away that the start date may be at risk, and you decide whether to move it.

**Draft warning to you, if needed**
> The background check for [new hire] has not cleared as of [date]. Accounts can't be created until it does, and the start date of [date] is at risk. Options: wait and keep the date, or ask the HR director to move it. Which would you like?

**Proof:** the dated clearance record, or a log of the check's status.

## Step 10. Onboarding and training plan
- **Onboarding checklist:** paperwork, introductions to Grace and Paul, a workspace, and a first-day schedule. Account-dependent items are marked "blocked until background check clears."
- **Payroll setup** stays with payroll and HR.
- **Training plan (first 30/60/90 days):** the payroll system and its processes, the cycle calendar, shadowing a full pay cycle, then supervised processing, then independent processing with review. Grace signs off on the plan.

**Proof:** the checklist and plan saved to the record, with owners and dates.

## Step 11. Report to you and record the chain

**Draft report**
> **R-114 Payroll Coordinator: status [date]**
> - Requirements on file; all 12 applicants screened (table attached).
> - Interviews held: [n]. Hiring decision: [candidate], made by Grace Obi on [date].
> - Offer: approved by [HR director]; sent by [name] on [date]. Signed acceptance matches approved terms [yes/no].
> - Record entered and read back. Pay and bank setup requested from payroll on [date].
> - Background check: [pending/cleared on date]. Accounts: [not created/created on date].
> - Onboarding and training plan ready.
> - **Waiting on:** [person/step].

The whole chain is recorded: requirements, screening table, kit, invites, scores and decision, approved offer, signed-offer comparison, record read-back, clearance, plan.

If a candidate or new hire raises a concern about how they were treated at any point, I send it to HR under HR 220.

## What I'm doing right now
I start Step 2 by opening the 12 applications and building the screening table. I'll send you that table, along with drafted clarifying questions for any "unclear" applicants, before contacting a single candidate.

I have not yet opened the 12 applications, so nothing below describes results. I'll start with step 1 and report real findings. Nothing goes to candidates, the HR director, payroll or IT without the approvals noted.

## Step 1: Screen all 12 against the two written must-haves only
**What I do:** Read each application and mark each must-have **Meets / Does not meet / Unclear**, with a short quote from the résumé as evidence.
- (1) 2+ years processing payroll
- (2) Experience with a payroll system for 50+ employees

I don't add criteria such as degree, certifications or employer prestige. I don't use age, name, gaps or anything else unrelated to the must-haves. If a résumé doesn't state headcount or duration, it's **Unclear**, not a rejection.

**Proof:** A 12-row screening sheet (candidate, must-have 1, must-have 2, quote, status). The totals check: Meets + Does not meet + Unclear = 12.

**Handoff:** Sheet goes to you for review.

## Step 2: Clarify the "Unclear" candidates
**What I do:** Draft this email for each unclear candidate. I send it after you OK the batch.

> Subject: Your application for Payroll Coordinator – a quick question
>
> Hello [Name],
>
> Thank you for applying for the Payroll Coordinator role at Wrenfield Clinics. To make sure we assess your application accurately, could you reply with two details?
> 1. How many years have you spent directly processing payroll?
> 2. Which payroll system(s) have you used, and roughly how many employees were paid through it?
>
> Please reply by [date, 3 business days out]. Thank you,
> [Owner name], HR, Wrenfield Clinics

**Proof:** Sent emails and replies, with the sheet updated and each change dated.

## Step 3: Shortlist to the hiring manager
**What I do:** Send Grace Obi the list of candidates who meet both must-haves, with the evidence. I don't pick the hire and I don't rank.

**Handoff:** Grace decides whom to interview. You decide on rejections. Anyone who "does not meet" gets a courteous decline only after you approve the wording.

## Step 4: Schedule interviews
**What I do:** Check Grace's and Paul Reyes's calendars, propose slots, and send invites once you confirm. Candidate invite:

> Subject: Interview invitation – Payroll Coordinator, Wrenfield Clinics
>
> Hello [Name], we'd like to invite you to interview for the Payroll Coordinator role with Grace Obi and Paul Reyes on [date/time], [location/video link], about [duration]. Please confirm, and let us know if you need any accommodation. Regards, [Owner name]

I also prepare an interview kit: the same questions for every candidate and a scorecard tied to the two must-haves and the job duties.

**Proof:** Calendar invites, candidate confirmations, and the kit file.

**Handoff:** Grace and Paul conduct the interviews and complete their scorecards.

## Step 5: Collect scorecards and Grace's decision
**What I do:** Compile both panelists' scorecards side by side and summarize where they agree and differ. I make no recommendation to override them.

**Proof:** Scorecards and Grace's written selection (an email is fine).

**Handoff:** **Grace chooses.** Reference checks are done by a person, or by me drafting the request after you approve, and only with the candidate's permission.

## Step 6: Offer approval and offer
**What I do:** Send you a request for the HR director. The director must approve the terms before anything goes to the candidate:

> To: [HR Director] — Approval request: R-114 Payroll Coordinator offer
> Grace Obi has selected [Candidate]. Please approve or amend: title, pay rate/salary, start date, schedule, benefits eligibility, and any conditions (background check). Scorecards are attached. I will not issue any offer until your approval is on file.

After approval, I prepare the offer letter from the approved terms only and check it line by line against the approval. You send it, or I send it with your OK. If the candidate counters, it goes back to the HR director. I can't improvise terms.

**Proof:** The director's written approval, the offer letter, and the match check showing every term identical.

## Step 7: Background check
**What I do:** The offer is contingent on the check. After acceptance, I prepare the check request and the candidate's consent form. The candidate authorizes it through the vendor.

**Proof:** The signed offer, the consent, and the vendor's result.

**Handoff:** A person reviews the result. If anything adverse appears, I stop. You and the HR director handle it, including any required notice process. I don't judge it.

## Step 8: Only after the check clears, set up the new hire
- **Accounts:** After the check clears, I file the IT request for email and the systems the role needs. Nothing is created before then.
- **Payroll:** I send payroll the approved offer terms and start date. **Payroll sets up pay and bank details.** I don't enter them. The new hire gives bank details through payroll's own secure process, not by email to me.

**Proof:** The clearance record dated before the IT ticket, the ticket numbers, and payroll's confirmation that setup is complete.

## Step 9: First day
**What I do:** Send the welcome email (arrival time, location, who to ask for, what to bring). I also put Grace's first-day schedule on the calendar and prepare a checklist: accounts working, paperwork, introductions to Grace and Paul. Once the hire has accepted and cleared, I draft decline notes to the remaining interviewees for your approval.

**Proof:** Completed first-day checklist, confirmation from IT and payroll, and the screening sheet and decision records filed for the requisition.

**Handoff:** Grace takes the new hire from there.

## Stop points where I wait for a person
1. You: review the screening and approve candidate emails.
2. Grace: choose interviewees and the hire.
3. HR director: approve the offer.
4. A person: review the background check result.
5. Payroll: set up pay and bank details.
6. IT: create the accounts.

**Next step now:** I'll start the screening sheet and send it to you.

# R-114 Payroll Coordinator: plan and what I do today

I can run steps 1 to 4 now. Step 5 needs Grace Obi's decision, and everything after it depends on her decision, the HR director's approval, the candidate's signed acceptance, and the background check. I won't skip past any of those. Where I describe later steps, nothing has happened yet.

---

## Step 1. Requirements
**Status:** Written must-haves exist, so I can proceed.
1. 2 or more years processing payroll
2. Experience with a payroll system for 50 or more employees

**Proof:** I file these two lines, with the requisition number and Grace Obi as hiring manager, at the top of the R-114 hiring record. I add nothing to them, such as degrees or certifications. If someone wants a nice-to-have counted, it has to be written and approved first.

## Step 2. Screen the 12 applications
I read each application against the two must-haves only. I record the evidence quoted from the application, and I don't use or note names, photos, age, graduation dates, gaps, family status, or anything else that points to a protected trait.

**Rating rules:**
- **Meets:** the application shows it.
- **Not shown:** the application doesn't say. I don't reject on this. It becomes a question in the interview or a short written follow-up.
- **Does not meet:** the application shows less than the requirement, for example 1 year of payroll processing.

**Screening table (format; I fill it from the 12 applications):**

| App # | Must-have 1: 2+ yrs processing payroll (evidence quoted) | Must-have 2: payroll system, 50+ employees (evidence quoted) | Result | Open question |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1–12 | "…" | "…" | Meets / Not shown / Does not meet | … |

I haven't read the applications in this session, so I'm not filling in any rows from guesses. When the table is done, I send it to you and Grace. Anyone marked "Does not meet" is listed with the quoted reason so a person can check my reading. Nobody is sent a rejection yet. I'll ask you when and how you want those sent, after Grace's decision.

## Step 3. Interview kit (same for every candidate)

**Questions tied to the requirements:**
1. *(Req. 1)* Walk us through a full payroll cycle you personally processed from start to finish. How often was it run, and what were your steps?
2. *(Req. 1)* How many years have you processed payroll, and in what roles? What did you own versus review?
3. *(Req. 1)* Tell us about a payroll error you found or caused. What happened and how did you correct it?
4. *(Req. 2)* Which payroll system(s) did you use? Approximately how many employees were paid through it?
5. *(Req. 2)* Which tasks did you do in that system yourself: entering hours, adjustments, deductions, reports, year-end filings?
6. *(Both)* Describe a time you had a deadline and incomplete data from a department. What did you do?

**Scoring guide (each question, 1–4):**
- **4:** Specific, first-hand, complete example. Clearly meets the requirement.
- **3:** Specific example with minor gaps. Meets the requirement.
- **2:** General or partly first-hand. Unclear whether the requirement is met.
- **1:** No relevant example, or the requirement is not met.

Each interviewer scores independently and writes one line of evidence per score. Scores are based on answers only, with no comparison across candidates during the interview and no notes on personal characteristics. The same questions are asked in the same order to everyone.

**Proof:** The kit is filed in the hiring record before any interview happens.

## Step 4. Schedule
**Panel:** Grace Obi and Paul Reyes, both required. I check both calendars for shared openings and offer each candidate times in the candidate's own time zone. Each candidate gets a separate invite, and candidates can't see each other's names.

**Draft invite (one per candidate):**

> Subject: Interview for Payroll Coordinator at Wrenfield Clinics
>
> Hello [first name],
>
> Thank you for applying for the Payroll Coordinator role. We'd like to invite you to an interview with Grace Obi (hiring manager) and Paul Reyes.
>
> Please choose one of these times, shown in [candidate time zone]:
> – [Option 1]
> – [Option 2]
> – [Option 3]
>
> The interview will last about [45] minutes by [video/in person]. We'll ask about your payroll processing experience and the payroll systems you've used.
>
> If you need any adjustment to take part, reply to this message and we'll work with you.
>
> Wrenfield Clinics HR

**Hand-off:** I send the invites only to candidates the screen shows as "Meets" or "Not shown." Before sending, I ask you to confirm that list, since a person should sign off on who moves forward. I send nothing before your confirmation.

**Proof:** The calendar entries and the sent invites are logged in the record.

## Step 5. A person decides: Grace Obi
After the interviews, I collect Grace's and Paul's scores and evidence lines and put them in a summary for Grace:

| Candidate | Q1–Q6 scores: Grace | Q1–Q6 scores: Paul | Evidence notes | Must-haves confirmed? | Open items |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

I **don't recommend or pick a hire**, and I won't "take the top score." If scores differ a lot between the two interviewers, I point that out and leave the resolution to Grace.

**Proof:** Grace's decision, in writing (email or chat), naming the candidate. It is filed in the record. Until I have it, I do not go to step 6.

## Step 6. Offer draft
I draft the offer only from terms the **HR director has approved in writing** (title, pay, start date, and so on). I don't write in any term that isn't in that approval. If the approval is missing, or if the pay or start date isn't in it, I stop and ask. I hand the draft to the approver, and **a person sends it**. I don't send it. I also don't set, suggest, or adjust pay.

**Proof:** The approved terms, the draft, and the approver's confirmation of it, all filed.

## Step 7. Signed acceptance
When the signed offer comes back, I compare it with the approved offer term by term: title, pay, start date, manager, location, conditions.

- **Match:** I go on to step 8.
- **Any change** (pay, start date, title, anything else): I stop. I tell you and the HR director that this is a new negotiation and needs a person and a new approval. I enter nothing in the record.

**Proof:** A side-by-side comparison table in the record.

## Step 8. Set up the record
From the signed, matching offer, I enter only job details: title, manager (Grace Obi), department, location, start date. I read the record back and file the read-back.

**Not mine:** pay and bank details are set up by payroll. I send payroll a request in the team chat:

> Payroll team: [new hire] has a signed, approved offer for Payroll Coordinator, start date [date]. Please set up pay and bank details per the approved offer on file. I haven't entered anything about pay or banking. – Wrenfield HR agent

## Step 9. Conditions: background check
The offer is conditional on a background check. **No accounts are created until it clears.** That covers email, payroll or HR system logins, and the chat. If the check isn't cleared by [start date minus lead time for account setup], I tell you right away that the start date is at risk and let you decide what to do, such as moving the date. I don't change the date myself, since it is in the approved offer.

**Proof:** The clearance notice in the record, dated before any account request.

## Step 10. Onboarding and training plan
After the check clears:
- **Onboarding:** first-day schedule, meetings with Grace and Paul, account requests to IT, paperwork list, and who the new hire meets in payroll.
- **Training plan:** the first 30/60/90 days, based on the gaps seen in the interview answers (for example, if the candidate's payroll system differs from Wrenfield's). I give the plan to Grace for review.

**Proof:** The onboarding checklist and the training plan, both filed.

## Step 11. Report to you
This is the report I'd send you at each stop, with the final one at day one:

> **R-114 Payroll Coordinator – status, [date]**
> – **Where it stands:** [step, e.g., screening done: X meet, Y not shown, Z do not meet]
> – **Waiting on:** [Grace: decision / HR director: offer approval / candidate: signed acceptance / background check vendor / payroll: pay setup]
> – **Risks:** [e.g., start date at risk if the check isn't cleared by …]
> – **Record:** all proof is in the R-114 hiring record: requirements, screening table, interview kit, invites, score summary, Grace's decision, approved and signed offers with comparison, record read-back, check clearance, onboarding and training plan.

## Throughout
- If a candidate or new hire raises a concern about how they were treated, I pass it to HR under HR 220 right away and don't try to resolve it myself.
- If any step fails, I go back to it and don't move ahead.

---

**Right now I'm starting step 2, and I'll send you the screening table once the 12 applications are read.** I need one thing from you: confirm that I may send interview invites to the candidates you approve after you see that table.

# R-114 Payroll Coordinator: plan from applications to day one

I work in order, keep the proof of each step in the R-114 hiring record, and stop wherever a person decides. I'm starting steps 1 and 2 now. Everything after that is staged and waits on the hand-offs below.

---

## Step 1. Requirements
**Done.** The written must-haves are on the requisition:
1. 2 or more years processing payroll
2. Experience with a payroll system for 50 or more employees

**Proof:** the requirement text, copied into the hiring record with the requisition number and today's date (Nov 4, 2026).

I'll apply both as written and won't add criteria. Must-have 2 could be read two ways: the system itself supports 50+ employees, or the candidate used it for a workforce of 50+. I'll accept either reading when the application shows it. If an application is silent, I'll mark it "unclear" rather than "does not meet".

---

## Step 2. Screen the 12 applications
I check each application against both must-haves and quote the evidence, such as the job title and dates or the system and headcount. I don't use or record anything about protected traits (age, sex, race, religion, disability, family status, national origin, and so on). Applicants are listed by application ID.

**Format of the screening table (I haven't filled it in here, so no results are shown):**

| App ID | Must-have 1: 2+ yrs processing payroll (evidence, source) | Must-have 2: payroll system, 50+ employees (evidence, source) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| R114-01 | e.g. "Payroll Clerk, Mar 2021–present, biweekly payroll" (résumé p.1) | e.g. "Used [system] for ~120 staff" (cover letter) | Meets both / Does not meet [which] / Unclear [what's missing] |
| … through R114-12 | | | |

- **Meets both** goes to the interview step.
- **Does not meet** is recorded with the specific reason tied to the must-have.
- **Unclear** gets a short factual question to the applicant, for example: "Your application lists payroll duties from 2022 to 2024. Roughly how many employees were on the payroll you processed, and which system did you use?" I only send it after you approve the wording, because it's the first contact with applicants.

**Proof:** the completed 12-row table in the hiring record, with counts (meets / does not meet / unclear).
**Hand-off:** I send you the table. You confirm the interview list before I contact anyone.

---

## Step 3. Interview kit
The same questions, the same order, and the same scoring guide for every candidate, each tied to a requirement.

**Questions**
1. (Req 1) Walk us through a full payroll cycle you ran from start to finish. How often, how many people, and what were your checkpoints?
2. (Req 1) Tell us about a payroll error you found or caused. What was it, how did you fix it, and what changed afterward?
3. (Req 2) Which payroll system(s) have you used, and for roughly how many employees? What did you do in it yourself?
4. (Req 2) Describe how you handled a change that affected many employees at once, such as a tax table update, a pay-rate change, or a new deduction.
5. (Req 1/2) How do you handle payroll data that is confidential? Give a specific example.

**Scoring guide (each question, 1–5, same for both interviewers)**
- 5: Specific, first-hand, with numbers or outcomes; clearly exceeds the requirement
- 4: Specific and first-hand; fully meets the requirement
- 3: Meets the minimum, but somewhat general
- 2: Vague or mostly second-hand; partly meets
- 1: No relevant example, or doesn't meet the requirement

Interviewers record a score and a one-line evidence note per question. No notes on anything unrelated to the requirements.

**Proof:** the kit saved to the record.
**Hand-off:** Grace and Paul review and may edit the kit before use.

---

## Step 4. Schedule
- **Panel required:** Grace Obi and Paul Reyes, both in each interview. I won't schedule a candidate with only one of them.
- I check both calendars for shared openings, then offer each candidate options expressed in the **candidate's time zone**.
- **Separate invites** per candidate. No invite lists other candidates.

**Draft invite (needs your approval of the first send):**
> Subject: Interview for Payroll Coordinator at Wrenfield Clinics
>
> Hello [Name],
>
> Thank you for applying for the Payroll Coordinator role. We'd like to invite you to a [45]-minute interview with Grace Obi (hiring manager) and Paul Reyes.
>
> Available times, in your time zone ([TZ]):
> – [Option 1]
> – [Option 2]
> – [Option 3]
>
> Please reply with the time that suits you, and we'll send a calendar invitation with the [location/video link].
>
> Wrenfield Clinics HR

**Proof:** confirmed invites, with both panelists accepted, logged per candidate.

---

## Step 5. A person decides
After the interviews I collect Grace's and Paul's scores and evidence notes into one summary.

**Summary format (to Grace, copy to you):**

| Candidate | Grace: Q1–Q5 | Paul: Q1–Q5 | Totals | Evidence highlights | Must-haves confirmed in interview? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

I add notes on where the two interviewers' scores differ by 2 or more points, so they can discuss it.

**Message to Grace:**
> Grace, here are the R-114 interview scores for all candidates, with evidence notes and where your scores and Paul's differ. Please tell me in writing which candidate you choose to hire, or if you want more interviews. I haven't ranked or recommended anyone. Once I have your decision, I'll prepare the offer request for the HR director's approval.

**I stop here.** Even if you ask me to "just take the top score," I won't pick the hire. The rule is that the hiring manager chooses.
**Proof:** Grace's written decision, saved to the record.

---

## Step 6. Offer draft
I can only draft from an offer the **HR director has approved**. I don't have approved terms yet, so I'd stop and ask.

**Message to the HR director (via you):**
> For R-114, Grace Obi has chosen [candidate]. Please approve the offer terms below, or send me the terms you approve: title, manager, department, location, start date, pay, any conditions (including the background check). I'll draft the offer letter strictly from what you approve.

I won't suggest pay, since anything that sets pay is a person's call. After approval I draft the letter using the approved terms word for word, include the background-check condition, and hand it to the approver. **A person sends it, not me.**
**Proof:** the HR director's approval and the draft next to it.

---

## Step 7. Signed acceptance
When the signed offer comes back, I compare it with the approved offer **term by term**: title, pay, start date, manager, location, conditions.

- **All match:** I record it and move to step 8.
- **Anything differs** (pay, start date, title, or a crossed-out condition): I stop. That's a new negotiation for a person and needs a new approval. I tell you which term changed and do nothing further on the record.

**Proof:** a comparison table, approved vs signed, with a match/no match mark per term.

---

## Step 8. Set up the record
From the signed, matching offer only, I enter: job title, manager (Grace Obi), department, location, start date. Then I read the record back and attach the read-back.

**Not me:** pay and bank details. I send payroll a request to set them up:
> Payroll team: R-114's hire [name] has signed an approved offer with a start date of [date]. Please set up pay and bank details per the approved offer. I haven't entered any pay or bank information.

**Proof:** the read-back of the record, and the request sent to payroll.

---

## Step 9. Conditions
New-hire accounts (email, payroll system, and so on) are created **only after the background check clears**. Until then:
- I make no account requests to IT.
- I track the check's status with whoever runs it.
- If a delay would hit the start date, I tell you right away:
> The background check for [name] hasn't cleared as of [date]. Their accounts can't be created until it does, and their start date is [date]. Options: wait for it to clear, or have a person decide whether to move the start date. I'm not changing the date myself.

**Proof:** the check's cleared status, with date, in the record, before any account is requested.

---

## Step 10. Onboarding and training plan
- **Onboarding:** a day-one checklist covering the welcome, paperwork, meeting Grace and Paul, building access, and the account setup that follows once cleared. Items needing accounts are marked "after clearance."
- **Training plan:** first 30/60/90 days, built from the role's requirements. It covers Wrenfield's payroll system and calendar, the review and approval steps, and handling confidential data. The training owner for each item is Grace or Paul, and I won't add pay-related items.

**Hand-off:** Grace approves both before the new hire sees them.
**Proof:** the checklist and plan saved in the record, with Grace's approval.

---

## Step 11. Report and record
**Report to you:**
> **R-114 Payroll Coordinator, status as of [date]**
> – Applications: 12 screened; [x] advanced, [y] not meeting, [z] clarified
> – Interviews: [n] held (Grace + Paul on all)
> – Hiring decision: [candidate], chosen by Grace Obi on [date]
> – Offer: approved by [HR director] on [date]; sent by [person]; signed on [date]; matches approved offer: [yes/no]
> – Record: entered and read back on [date]; pay and bank with payroll (status: [ ])
> – Background check: [pending/cleared on date]; accounts: [held/created]
> – Start date: [date], [on track/at risk because …]
> – Waiting on: [person] for [item]

I log the full chain (requirements, table, kit, invites, scores, Grace's decision, approval, comparison, read-back, clearance, plans) in the hiring record so anyone can follow it.

**Throughout:** if any candidate or new hire raises a concern about how they were treated, I send it to HR under HR 220 right away, and I don't try to resolve it myself.

---

## Where a person acts
| Step | Person |
|---|---|
| 2 | You: confirm interview list and applicant questions |
| 3 | Grace and Paul: review kit |
| 5 | **Grace: decides the hire** |
| 6 | **HR director: approves offer; a person sends it** |
| 7 | You and HR director, if the candidate changed anything |
| 8 | Payroll: pay and bank details |
| 9 | Background-check provider/HR: clearance; you: any start-date change |
| 10 | Grace: approves onboarding and training plans |

**Scoring:** 1–5 per question.  
- 1 = No relevant evidence or answer does not meet the requirement.  
- 2 = Limited evidence; significant gaps.  
- 3 = Meets the basic requirement.  
- 4 = Strong evidence; handled similar work independently.  
- 5 = Exceptional evidence; high-volume payroll experience, strong controls, clear examples.

### Question 1 — Payroll processing experience  
“Please walk us through your hands-on payroll processing experience, including how long you have processed payroll, the payroll cycle you supported, and your responsibilities from data collection through final review.”

**Requirement tested:** 2 or more years processing payroll.  
**Scoring guide:**  
- 1: No payroll processing experience.  
- 3: At least 2 years processing payroll with clear responsibilities.  
- 5: More than 2 years with strong ownership of payroll cycles, reviews, and issue resolution.

### Question 2 — Payroll system and employee volume  
“Tell us about the payroll system or systems you have used, the approximate employee count supported, and what tasks you performed in the system.”

**Requirement tested:** Experience with a payroll system for 50 or more employees.  
**Scoring guide:**  
- 1: No payroll system experience.  
- 3: Used a payroll system for 50+ employees.  
- 5: Used payroll systems for 50+ employees with strong knowledge of setup, processing, reporting, and troubleshooting.

### Question 3 — Accuracy and deadlines  
“Describe a time you had to complete payroll accurately under a deadline. What checks did you use before payroll was finalized?”

**Requirement tested:** Payroll processing capability.  
**Scoring guide:**  
- 1: No clear controls or process.  
- 3: Uses basic review steps and meets deadlines.  
- 5: Uses structured controls, reconciliations, exception checks, and clear escalation.

### Question 4 — Payroll issue resolution  
“Tell us about a payroll error or discrepancy you helped resolve. What happened, what did you do, and what was the result?”

**Requirement tested:** Payroll processing experience and judgment.  
**Scoring guide:**  
- 1: No relevant example.  
- 3: Provides a reasonable example with appropriate correction steps.  
- 5: Shows careful investigation, documentation, communication, and prevention.

### Question 5 — Confidentiality and sensitive information  
“Payroll work involves confidential employee information. How do you protect payroll data in your daily work?”

**Requirement tested:** Payroll role readiness.  
**Scoring guide:**  
- 1: Does not recognize confidentiality obligations.  
- 3: Understands confidentiality and basic secure handling.  
- 5: Gives strong examples of secure handling, access control, and discretion.

## 3. Build the interview kit

**R-114 Payroll Coordinator — Structured Interview Kit**  
**Role:** Payroll Coordinator  
**Hiring manager:** Grace Obi  
**Panel:** Grace Obi and Paul Reyes  
**Must-haves being tested:**
1. 2 or more years processing payroll.  
2. Experience with a payroll system for 50 or more employees.

### Candidate questions

1. **Payroll experience**
   - “Please walk us through your payroll processing experience over the last two or more years. What parts of the payroll cycle were you directly responsible for?”

2. **Payroll system and employee volume**
   - “Which payroll systems have you used, and approximately how many employees were included in the payrolls you worked on?”

3. **Payroll cycle process**
   - “Describe the steps you follow to process a payroll cycle from inputs through review and submission.”

4. **Payroll accuracy**
   - “Tell us about a time you found a payroll error before payroll was finalized. What did you do?”

5. **Payroll issue resolution**
   - “Tell us about a time an employee or manager raised a payroll question or discrepancy. How did you investigate and resolve it?”

6. **Controls and deadlines**
   - “How do you keep payroll work accurate and on schedule when there are late changes or competing deadlines?”

### Scoring guide

Each interviewer scores each question from 1 to 5.

| Score | Guide |
|---|---|
| 1 | Does not show relevant payroll processing experience or payroll system experience. |
| 2 | Shows limited or unclear experience; evidence does not fully support the must-have. |
| 3 | Meets the must-have; provides credible examples of payroll processing and system use. |
| 4 | Strong evidence; has handled multiple payroll cycles, payroll issues, and system tasks with limited supervision. |
| 5 | Exceptional evidence; has deep payroll cycle ownership, strong system experience, accuracy controls, and issue resolution experience. |

### Interviewer instructions

- Ask the same core questions of every candidate.  
- Follow-up questions may clarify answers but must stay job-related.  
- Do not ask about protected traits or non-job-related personal matters.  
- Enter scores and job-related notes only.  
- The hiring manager, Grace Obi, makes the hiring decision.

Subject: R-114 Payroll Coordinator — End-to-End Hiring Plan, Proof, and Handoffs

Hi [Owner],

I would take requisition R-114 from application review through the new hire’s first day using the process below. I would not make the hiring decision myself, I would not issue an offer unless it matches HR director approval, I would not set up pay or bank details, and I would not request new-hire system accounts until the background check clears.

## Role details

- Requisition: R-114
- Role: Payroll Coordinator
- Hiring manager: Grace Obi
- Interview panel: Grace Obi and Paul Reyes
- Must-haves:
  1. 2 or more years processing payroll
  2. Experience with a payroll system for 50 or more employees
- Total applications: 12

---

## Step-by-step process, proof, and handoffs

| Step | What I would do | Proof I would keep/show | Person handoff |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Confirm requisition requirements | Confirm R-114 details, must-haves, hiring manager, interview panel, and approval rules. | Requisition record showing R-114, job title, must-haves, Grace Obi as hiring manager, Grace Obi/Paul Reyes as panel. | None unless details are unclear; then hand off question to owner/Grace. |
| 2. Build screening rubric | Create a pass/fail screen based only on the written must-haves. | Screening rubric with two required criteria and notes field. | None. |
| 3. Review all 12 applications | Screen each application against the two must-haves. | Completed applicant screening matrix for all 12 applicants, with pass/fail and evidence from resume/application. | None. |
| 4. Identify qualified candidates | Mark candidates who meet both must-haves as “Qualified for hiring manager review.” Candidates missing either must-have are not advanced. | ATS status updates and screening matrix. | Handoff qualified slate to Grace Obi. |
| 5. Send qualified slate to hiring manager | Send Grace the qualified candidates and the screening evidence. | Email/slack message to Grace with candidate list and screening matrix attached/linked. | Grace reviews the qualified slate. |
| 6. Schedule interviews | Coordinate interviews with qualified candidates, Grace, and Paul. | Calendar invites, candidate confirmations, interview schedule. | Grace and Paul conduct interviews. |
| 7. Collect interview feedback | Send structured feedback form to Grace and Paul and collect responses. | Completed feedback forms/interview scorecards. | Grace and Paul provide feedback. |
| 8. Hiring manager chooses candidate | Ask Grace to select the candidate to hire or request additional interviews. | Written hiring decision from Grace in ATS/email. | Grace makes the hiring decision. |
| 9. Prepare offer approval request | Prepare proposed offer details for HR director approval. | Offer approval request containing candidate, role, comp, start date, and terms. | HR director approves or revises offer. |
| 10. Verify offer matches approval | Check final offer letter exactly matches HR director-approved terms. | Approved offer record and final offer letter comparison. | None unless mismatch; then return to HR director. |
| 11. Extend conditional offer | Send conditional offer to selected candidate, contingent on required checks. | Sent offer email/letter and candidate acceptance. | Candidate accepts or declines. |
| 12. Notify non-selected candidates | Send respectful disposition notices after offer stage is appropriate. | Sent rejection emails and ATS disposition records. | None. |
| 13. Initiate background check | After acceptance, send background check instructions/authorization. | Background check initiation record and candidate authorization. | Background check vendor/candidate. |
| 14. Wait for background clearance | Track background check status. Do not create accounts yet. | Background check result showing “clear” or equivalent. | If issue arises, hand off to HR lead/legal-compliance process. |
| 15. After clearance, start new-hire setup | Once cleared, notify IT/facilities/manager that onboarding can begin. | Background clearance confirmation and onboarding task list. | IT creates accounts; manager prepares first-day work plan. |
| 16. Payroll handoff | Send payroll the approved offer and new-hire details needed for setup. Payroll handles pay and bank details. | Payroll setup request, approved offer, start date, employee information. | Payroll sets up pay and bank details. |
| 17. Confirm first-day plan | Coordinate first-day schedule with Grace and send it to new hire. | First-day agenda, calendar invites, confirmation emails. | Grace owns day-one welcome and role-specific onboarding. |
| 18. First-day check-in | Confirm new hire arrived, has access after cleared setup, and knows where to go for payroll/benefits/onboarding tasks. | First-day completion checklist. | Grace continues onboarding; payroll/IT handle their domains. |

## 3. Build the interview kit

I would create one interview kit used for every candidate advanced from screening.

**Proof placed in record:** interview questions, scoring guide, and interviewer score form.

**Interview kit for R-114 — Payroll Coordinator**

**Instructions for Grace Obi and Paul Reyes:**  
Use the same questions for every candidate. Score based on job-related evidence only. Do not ask about or record protected traits.

### Question 1 — Payroll processing experience

“Please walk us through your hands-on payroll processing experience, including how long you have processed payroll, what parts of the payroll cycle you handled, and the pay frequencies you have worked with.”

**Tied requirement:** 2 or more years processing payroll.

**Score guide:**

- 5 — Clear 2+ years hands-on payroll processing experience, with end-to-end or substantial payroll cycle responsibility.
- 3 — At least 2 years payroll processing experience, but limited detail or narrower scope.
- 1 — Does not show 2 years hands-on payroll processing experience.

### Question 2 — Payroll system and employee volume

“What payroll systems have you used, and approximately how many employees were processed through those systems?”

**Tied requirement:** Experience with a payroll system for 50 or more employees.

**Score guide:**

- 5 — Direct payroll system experience for 50+ employees, with strong working knowledge.
- 3 — Payroll system experience for 50+ employees, but limited scope or detail.
- 1 — No clear payroll system experience for 50+ employees.

### Question 3 — Payroll accuracy scenario

“Tell us about a time you found or resolved a payroll discrepancy. What did you do, and what was the outcome?”

**Tied requirement:** Payroll processing experience.

**Score guide:**

- 5 — Gives a clear payroll-specific example showing accurate processing, investigation, and resolution.
- 3 — Gives a relevant example but with limited detail.
- 1 — No payroll-specific example or unclear role.

### Question 4 — Payroll system workflow

“Describe a payroll workflow you have used in a payroll system, from collecting or importing data through review and final submission.”

**Tied requirement:** Payroll system experience for 50+ employees.

**Score guide:**

- 5 — Demonstrates practical system workflow knowledge for a payroll population of 50+ employees.
- 3 — Demonstrates basic system workflow knowledge.
- 1 — Does not demonstrate practical payroll system workflow knowledge.

R-114 Interview Kit — Payroll Coordinator

Use the same core questions for every candidate. Score based only on job-related evidence. Do not ask about or record protected traits. If a candidate raises a concern about treatment or fairness, refer it to HR under HR 220.

## 3. Create the interview kit

**Action:** I create a standard interview kit to be used for every interviewed candidate. The questions are tied to the must-haves and scored the same way for everyone.

**Interview kit I would file and send to Grace Obi and Paul Reyes:**

Subject: Interview Kit for R-114 Payroll Coordinator

> **R-114 Payroll Coordinator — Standard Interview Kit**  
> Date prepared: November 4, 2026  
> Role: Payroll Coordinator  
> Hiring manager: Grace Obi  
> Interview panel: Grace Obi and Paul Reyes  
>
> **Written must-haves being assessed**  
> 1. 2 or more years processing payroll.  
> 2. Experience with a payroll system for 50 or more employees.  
>
> **Instructions for interviewers**  
> - Ask the same core questions of each candidate.  
> - Score based on job-related evidence only.  
> - Do not ask or record information about protected traits.  
> - Record examples and evidence, not impressions unrelated to the requirements.  
>
> **Core questions and scoring guide**
>
> **Question 1 — Payroll processing experience**  
> “Please walk us through your payroll processing experience, including the types of payroll cycles you have handled and your role in each step.”  
> Requirement assessed: 2 or more years processing payroll.  
> Score:  
> 1 = No clear payroll processing experience.  
> 2 = Limited exposure; less than 2 years or only assisted indirectly.  
> 3 = At least 2 years processing payroll with basic recurring responsibilities.  
> 4 = More than 2 years processing payroll with ownership of multiple recurring payroll tasks.  
> 5 = Extensive payroll processing ownership, including complex cycles, corrections, and deadline management.
>
> **Question 2 — Payroll system and employee volume**  
> “Tell us about the payroll systems you have used and the approximate employee counts supported in those systems.”  
> Requirement assessed: Experience with a payroll system for 50 or more employees.  
> Score:  
> 1 = No payroll system experience.  
> 2 = Payroll system exposure but under 50 employees or unclear volume.  
> 3 = Payroll system experience supporting 50+ employees.  
> 4 = Payroll system experience supporting 50+ employees with regular processing responsibility.  
> 5 = Strong payroll system experience supporting 50+ employees, including reporting, troubleshooting, corrections, or configuration support.
>
> **Question 3 — Payroll accuracy and issue resolution**  
> “Describe a payroll error or discrepancy you identified or helped resolve. What did you do, and what was the result?”  
> Requirements assessed: Payroll processing experience and practical payroll system use.  
> Score:  
> 1 = No relevant example.  
> 2 = Example is vague or candidate had minimal role.  
> 3 = Clear example showing basic payroll issue resolution.  
> 4 = Strong example showing accurate investigation, correction, and communication.  
> 5 = Excellent example showing ownership, prevention of repeat issues, and sound judgment.
>
> **Question 4 — Deadlines and confidentiality**  
> “Payroll work often involves strict deadlines and sensitive information. How have you managed payroll deadlines and confidential payroll information in prior roles?”  
> Requirements assessed: Practical payroll processing experience.  
> Score:  
> 1 = No relevant payroll deadline/confidentiality experience.  
> 2 = Limited or unclear example.  
> 3 = Adequate example of managing deadlines and confidentiality.  
> 4 = Strong example showing reliable process and discretion.  
> 5 = Excellent example showing disciplined controls, confidentiality, and consistent deadline performance.
>
> **Overall recommendation options**  
> - Strongly recommend advancing  
> - Recommend advancing  
> - Mixed / discuss  
> - Do not recommend advancing  
>
> **Interviewer score sheet**  
> Candidate:  
> Interviewer:  
> Date:  
> Q1 score and evidence:  
> Q2 score and evidence:  
> Q3 score and evidence:  
> Q4 score and evidence:  
> Overall recommendation:  
> Job-related comments:

**Proof:** Interview kit with questions and scoring guide.

Subject: R-114 Payroll Coordinator — Interview Kit

## 11. Training plan for Payroll Coordinator

**Action:** I create a role-specific training plan and send it to Grace for use with the new hire.

**Training plan I would send to Grace:**

Subject: R-114 Payroll Coordinator — Training Plan for [New Hire Name]

> Hi Grace,  
>
> Below is the proposed training plan for [New Hire Name], Payroll Coordinator. It is tied to the role requirements and first-day onboarding. Please adjust with any Wrenfield-specific process owners or dates.  
>
> **Payroll Coordinator Training Plan**
>
> **Week 1 — Orientation and core process overview**  
> Goals: Understand Wrenfield payroll calendar, confidentiality expectations, payroll system access, and team workflows.  
> Activities:  
> - Review payroll calendar and processing deadlines.  
> - Review confidentiality and data-handling expectations.  
> - Complete payroll system orientation, once accounts/access are active.  
> - Shadow current payroll processing workflow.  
> - Meet key contacts: Grace Obi, payroll team, HR/payroll handoff contacts.  
> Evidence of completion: signed/acknowledged policy review, manager check-in notes.
>
> **Weeks 2–3 — Guided payroll processing tasks**  
> Goals: Perform recurring payroll tasks with supervision.  
> Activities:  
> - Review employee data inputs and change controls.  
> - Practice payroll system navigation and standard reports.  
> - Assist with payroll-cycle preparation.  
> - Review discrepancy identification and escalation process.  
> Evidence of completion: supervisor confirmation of guided task completion.
>
> **Weeks 4–6 — Increased ownership**  
> Goals: Handle assigned payroll process steps with review.  
> Activities:  
> - Own assigned payroll-cycle checklist items.  
> - Prepare standard payroll reports.  
> - Document questions and process gaps.  
> - Participate in post-payroll review.  
> Evidence of completion: Grace’s review of assigned checklist items and feedback.
>
> **By 60–90 days — Role effectiveness check**  
> Goals: Confirm the new hire can reliably support payroll processing for Wrenfield’s employee population.  
> Activities:  
> - Review performance against payroll deadlines, accuracy, system use, and confidentiality expectations.  
> - Identify any additional training needs.  
> - Confirm ongoing responsibilities.  
> Evidence of completion: manager check-in summary.
>
> Thank you.
